name: Tiger Trap
label: K
lede: A year, four friends from Sacramento, one album that outsold everything K Records had put out so far.

eras.title: Olympia, then Sacramento
eras.text: Rose Melberg goes to a K Records festival in Olympia, comes home to Sacramento and starts a band with her high school friend. Within weeks they have a split single out.

years.src: KEXP: Throwaway Style · Wikipedia: Rose Melberg
years.h: Rose Melberg goes to the International Pop Underground Convention
years.p: The K Records festival in Olympia, Washington is where the idea of a band of her own takes hold. She is just out of high school.
years.xp: KEXP's Softies feature says [[Rose Melberg|1206e9c0-a650-4e2d-bd7c-6bc1ae260634]] formed Tiger Trap after attending the 1991 International Pop Underground Convention. Wikipedia dates her appearance there to August 1991, right after high school.

years.cap: Tiger Trap: Rose Melberg, Angela Loy, Jen Braun, Heather Dunn
years.src: Wikipedia: Tiger Trap · Trouser Press · KEXP: Throwaway Style
years.h: Four Sacramento friends become Tiger Trap
years.p: [[Rose Melberg|1206e9c0-a650-4e2d-bd7c-6bc1ae260634]] and her high school friend Angela Loy add bassist Jen Braun and drummer Heather Dunn. Braun came from the Tower Records where Melberg worked.
years.xp:
Wikipedia says Braun was recruited through a shared job at Tower Records and Dunn was introduced by a mutual recommendation. Trouser Press has it that the band formed at a Flaming Lips show.

The name is a point of dispute. Trouser Press says it came from a Beat Happening song; KEXP says it came from a Calvin and Hobbes comic strip and that the Beat Happening story is a common mistake.

years.h: Split single with Bratmobile: Words and Smiles
years.p: Tiger Trap's first record is a split on the Four Letter Words label, out within weeks of the band forming, with Olympia's Bratmobile on the other side.
years.xp: The song "Words and Smiles" is one KEXP singles out as capturing the rush of a crush. Wikipedia says the split appeared within weeks of the band's formation.

years.h: "Supercrush" is Tiger Trap's first record for K
years.p: Wikipedia lists the K single as 1992. The song reappears on the album as "Super Crush".

eras.title: One album, ten thousand copies
eras.text: Calvin Johnson takes the band to Seattle for a record that becomes K's best seller. A five-song EP follows and the band plays its last show that December.

years.src: Wikipedia: Tiger Trap (album) · KEXP: Throwaway Style · KCSB: Tape Quarantine
years.h: Tiger Trap: twelve songs, about thirty minutes
years.p: [[Calvin Johnson|cac7a688-14a8-46c3-8fc8-11cca866677c]] produced it at Avast! Studios in Seattle. Heather Lewis of [[Beat Happening|449e44cb-bcae-4c48-a1af-5d8df0f81456]] did the cover.
years.xp:
The opener is "Puzzle Pieces"; other songs include "You're Sleeping", "Eight Wheels", "Chester" and "Prettiest Boy". KCSB called it a record whose stakes are to dance and nothing more.

NPR's Maria Sherman heard sugar-sweet punk closer to Talulah Gosh than to the riot grrrl bands around it. Spin praised the melodies and the Chicago Tribune the three-part harmonies.

years.src: Wikipedia: Tiger Trap (album) · Wikipedia: Tiger Trap
years.h: About 10,000 copies, K's biggest seller until Beck
years.p: Wikipedia's album page says Tiger Trap was K Records' best-selling release until Beck's One Foot in the Grave arrived in 1994.
years.xp: Wikipedia's band page puts the sales at about 10,000, a single-source figure. The band that got it had existed for roughly a year.

years.h: Sour Grass: a five-song EP is the last record
years.p: Trouser Press lists it as the final Tiger Trap release, on K.

years.cap: Bottom of the Hill, San Francisco
years.h: Last show at Bottom of the Hill, San Francisco
years.p: Wikipedia puts the final concert in December 1993, about a year after the band formed.

eras.title: The band ends badly, the Softies begin
eras.text: The breakup was not friendly. A fan at a Sacramento show becomes Melberg's next bandmate.

years.src: Wikipedia: The Softies · KEXP: Throwaway Style
years.h: Tiger Trap breaks up, and KEXP says not on good terms
years.p: Wikipedia's Softies page dates the split to January 1994.
years.xp:
KEXP says the band disbanded acrimoniously. Melberg told the site the attention came fast and "we were not really prepared".

No source we found gives the specific reasons, so this page does not either.

years.src: Wikipedia: The Softies · KEXP: Throwaway Style · Trouser Press · Wikipedia: Tiger Trap
years.h: Jen Sbragia and Melberg start the Softies
years.p: [[Jen Sbragia|fa10b28a-aa6c-4991-a8aa-12d60746cc29]] met Melberg at a Tiger Trap show in Sacramento and got in touch after the band ended. The [[The Softies|3daebde2-4630-40d8-be75-438edea4b281]] duo followed, with a K single, "He'll Never Have To Know", and an LP, It's Love, both in 1995.
years.xp:
Wikipedia lists Calvin Johnson as producer of the single. KEXP says Sbragia "really seemed like she was zoning in on me" at the show, per Melberg. The pair later moved to Portland.

Melberg also went on to Go Sailor and Gaze, where she played drums. Heather Dunn drummed for Lois, the reformed Raincoats and Dub Narcotic Sound System.

eras.title: The gateway twee record
eras.text: A one-year band stays in print and in conversation. Writers keep pointing new listeners at the album.

years.h: Pitchfork's "Twee as Fuck" essay recommends Tiger Trap
years.p: Wikipedia's album page cites the 2005 Pitchfork piece as highly recommending the record.

years.src: Wikipedia: Tiger Trap (album) · Wikipedia: Tiger Trap
years.h: The A.V. Club names it a gateway
years.p: By 2014 The A.V. Club was steering new listeners to the album as an entry point to twee.
years.xp: Wikipedia's page also notes Complex ranking it No. 40 among the 50 best indie rock albums of the 1990s. Rob Sheffield called the band "a pioneering indie-pop outfit of four women".
